question:
Choose the word that means the same as the given word.

Calamity
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Debacle.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Calamity" means a great misfortune, a disaster or an event causing sudden and serious damage. (आपदा / विपत्ति)

• "Debacle" means a sudden, complete and humiliating collapse or failure; a disaster. It is therefore the closest synonym of "calamity".

◦ Example: The flood was a calamity/debacle for the entire district.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Embark" means to board a ship/aircraft or to begin a new venture — unrelated to a disaster.

• Option 2 "Debauchery" means excessive indulgence in sensual pleasures (व्यभिचार) — a moral term, not a disaster.

• Option 3 "Debar" means to officially bar or exclude someone from something (वंचित करना).

NOTE

• Synonyms of calamity: disaster, catastrophe, debacle, misfortune, adversity, cataclysm.

• Antonyms of calamity: blessing, boon, good fortune, benefit.

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

David said that statistics are his favourite subject.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. statistics are his.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Nouns ending in -ics (statistics, mathematics, physics, economics, politics, ethics) are plural in form but singular in meaning when they denote a subject/branch of study. They therefore take a singular verb.

• Here "statistics" is clearly a school subject ("his favourite subject"), so the verb must be "is", not "are".

◦ Correct: David said that statistics is his favourite subject.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "David said that" is correct — reported speech introduced by "said that".

• Option 2 "favourite subject" is correct (British spelling "favourite" is acceptable).

• Option 3 "No error" cannot be chosen because a clear subject–verb agreement error exists.

NOTE

• The same word can be plural when it means data/figures: "The statistics are misleading."

• Similar rule: "Mathematics is an interesting subject", "Physics is difficult", "Economics is my optional paper".

question:
Select the appropriate synonym for the underlined word.

The child develops a deadly disease.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. fatal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Deadly" means causing or likely to cause death; lethal. (प्राणघातक / जानलेवा)

• "Fatal" also means causing death, so it is the exact synonym in the context of a disease.

◦ Correct: The child develops a deadly/fatal disease.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "huge" means very large in size (विशाल) — it describes size, not lethality.

• Option 2 "corrective" means intended to correct or remedy something (सुधारात्मक) — the opposite idea.

• Option 3 "kind" means gentle and considerate (दयालु) — completely unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of deadly: fatal, lethal, mortal, terminal, malignant, life-threatening.

• Antonyms of deadly: harmless, benign, innocuous, wholesome, curative.

question:
Select the appropriate antonym for the underlined word.

Richard himself came up to persuade David to agree to their plan.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. deter.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Persuade" means to convince someone to do something by reasoning or urging. (मनाना / राज़ी करना)

• "Deter" means to discourage or prevent someone from doing something, which is the exact opposite of persuading. (रोकना / हतोत्साहित करना)

◦ Example: The heavy fine will deter people from breaking the rule.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "prompt" means to urge/encourage someone to act — a synonym, not an antonym.

• Option 2 "lure" means to tempt or entice someone — again close in sense to persuading.

• Option 3 "coax" means to gently persuade with flattery — a synonym of persuade.

NOTE

• Synonyms of persuade: convince, induce, coax, cajole, prevail upon, win over.

• Antonyms of persuade: deter, dissuade, discourage, forbid, prevent.

question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

John rushed to the spot and saw his wife and kid ______ on the road.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. lying.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After verbs of perception such as see, hear, watch, notice, feel, the structure is "see + object + V1 / V-ing". Here the continuous, ongoing state requires the present participle (V-ing).

• The intransitive verb "lie" (to be in a horizontal position) forms: lie – lay – lain – lying. So the correct participle is "lying".

◦ Correct: John rushed to the spot and saw his wife and kid lying on the road.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "lain" is the past participle (V3) and cannot follow "saw ... kid" directly.

• Option 3 "lie" (base form) would suggest a completed single action, which is unnatural here.

• Option 4 "laying" comes from "lay" (to put something down), a transitive verb needing an object — lay – laid – laid – laying.

NOTE

• Remember the pair: lie / lay / lain / lying = to recline (no object); lay / laid / laid / laying = to place something (needs an object).

• "The hen is laying eggs" vs. "The book is lying on the table".

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

When I have arrived at the theatre, the show had already started.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. When I have arrived at.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When two actions happen in the past, the earlier action takes the past perfect (had + V3) and the later action takes the simple past (V2).

• Here "the show had already started" is the earlier action, so the second clause must be in the simple past: "When I arrived at the theatre".

• The present perfect ("have arrived") can never be used with a past perfect in the same time frame, nor with a definite past reference.

◦ Correct: When I arrived at the theatre, the show had already started.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "had already started" is correct — the earlier past action.

• Option 3 "the theatre, the show" is correct.

• Option 4 "No error" is wrong because the tense error is clear.

NOTE

• Standard pattern: Simple Past + Past Perfect — "When I reached the station, the train had left."

• Adverbs like already, just, never sit between "had" and the past participle.

question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

The water from the river was ______ cold for me to drink directly.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. too.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The structure "too + adjective + to + V1" expresses that something is excessive to the point of preventing an action — it carries a negative result.

• The sentence means the water was so cold that drinking it directly was not possible, so "too cold to drink" is required.

◦ Correct: The water from the river was too cold for me to drink directly.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "very" merely intensifies ("very cold") and does not carry the "impossible to do" sense demanded by the "to drink" infinitive.

• Option 2 "most" is a superlative marker and needs "the" plus a comparison group.

• Option 4 "many" is used with countable plural nouns, not with an adjective like "cold".

NOTE

• Compare: "too ... to" = negative result ("too weak to walk" = cannot walk); "so ... that" = "He was so weak that he could not walk"; "enough to" = positive result ("strong enough to lift it").

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

The idea was to delivered governmental services at the citizen's doorstep.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. deliver government services.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After the infinitive marker "to", the base form (V1) of the verb is used. Hence "to delivered" is wrong and must become "to deliver".

• The standard collocation for public administration is "government services" (a noun used attributively), not "governmental services".

◦ Correct: The idea was to deliver government services at the citizen's doorstep.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "delivering government serviced" wrongly uses the gerund after "to" and turns "services" into the verb "serviced".

• Option 2 "delivers governmental servicing" wrongly uses the finite verb "delivers" after "to".

• Option 3 "No improvement" is wrong because "to delivered" is clearly ungrammatical.

NOTE

• "To + V1" (infinitive): to go, to deliver, to write. Do not confuse it with "to + V-ing" which occurs only after phrases such as "look forward to", "be used to", "with a view to", "object to".

question: Choose the incorrectly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Lattar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Lattar" is misspelt. The intended words are "latter" (the second of two things mentioned) or "letter" (a written message / a character of the alphabet). (उत्तरार्ध / पत्र)

• Spelling key: LAT + TER (latter) — there is no English word spelt "lattar".

◦ Example: Of tea and coffee, I prefer the latter.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Critical" (CRIT + I + CAL) — expressing adverse judgement or extremely important, is correctly spelt.

• "Mastery" (MAS + TER + Y) — complete command over a subject or skill, is correctly spelt.

• "Loudly" (LOUD + LY) — in a loud manner, is correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Watch the pair former (the first of two) and latter (the second of two). Also distinguish later (afterwards in time) from latter.

question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

Bell the cat
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. To do a dangerous task.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "bell the cat" means to undertake a risky or dangerous task, especially on behalf of a group. (खतरनाक काम अपने ज़िम्मे लेना)

• It comes from Aesop's fable in which the mice agreed that a bell should be tied round the cat's neck, but no mouse dared to do it.

◦ Example: Everyone wanted the manager's decision reversed, but who would bell the cat?

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "To estimate the risks involved" describes risk assessment, not actually performing the risky act.

• Option 3 "To reveal confidential information" corresponds to idioms such as "let the cat out of the bag" or "spill the beans".

• Option 4 "To train company's employees" has no idiomatic link with the phrase.

NOTE

• Other cat idioms: "let the cat out of the bag" (to disclose a secret), "a cat-and-mouse game" (repeated pursuit), "curiosity killed the cat" (excessive inquisitiveness is harmful).

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

Using a loofah with a hydrating / shower gel each day also ensures / you'll have the most smoothest skin.
option_1: shower gel each day also ensures
option_3: you'll have the most smoothest skin.
option_4: Using a loofah with a hydrating
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. you'll have the most smoothest skin.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Smoothest" is already the superlative degree of "smooth" (smooth – smoother – smoothest). Adding "most" before it creates a double superlative, which is always incorrect.

◦ Correct: ... you'll have the smoothest skin.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "shower gel each day also ensures" is correct — the gerund subject "Using a loofah ..." takes the singular verb "ensures".

• Option 2 "No error" cannot be chosen because of the double superlative.

• Option 4 "Using a loofah with a hydrating" is correct as the opening gerund phrase.

NOTE

• Never combine "more/most" with the "-er/-est" form: more better, most smoothest, most easiest are all wrong.

• One-syllable adjectives take -er/-est (smooth – smoother – smoothest); longer adjectives take more/most (beautiful – more beautiful – most beautiful).

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

She was bored because she didn't have any work to does.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. work to do.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After the infinitive marker "to", the base form (V1) of the verb must be used. Therefore "to does" is wrong and must become "to do".

• "Work" here is an uncountable noun, so it takes no plural "-s" and fits with "any".

◦ Correct: She was bored because she didn't have any work to do.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "work to done" wrongly uses the past participle after "to".

• Option 2 "No improvement" is wrong because "to does" is clearly ungrammatical.

• Option 4 "works to do" wrongly pluralises the uncountable noun "work".

NOTE

• Uncountable nouns commonly tested: work, information, advice, furniture, luggage, equipment, news, machinery. They take singular verbs and no plural "-s".

• "Works" is possible only in special senses (a factory, or literary/artistic creations — "the works of Tagore").

question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

Loaves and fishes
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Material gain.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "loaves and fishes" means material gains or personal profit — especially worldly benefits sought from a position, office or public service. (भौतिक लाभ)

• It alludes to the biblical miracle in which Jesus fed a multitude with five loaves and two fishes; the crowd followed him for the food rather than for his teaching.

◦ Example: He joined politics only for the loaves and fishes of office.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Accidently kill someone" has no connection with the phrase.

• Option 3 "To bury the dead" is a literal expression, not this idiom.

• Option 4 "To let bygones be bygones" means to forgive and forget past quarrels — a different idiom altogether.

NOTE

• Related idioms of profit-seeking: "feather one's nest" (to enrich oneself), "line one's pockets" (to make money dishonestly), "milk the cow" (to exploit for gain).

question: Choose the sentence with no spelling error.
option_1: I can't stop the tissue from repairing.
option_2: I can't stop the tissue from reparing.
option_3: I can't stop the tisue from repairing.
option_4: I can't stop the tissue from repayring.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. I can't stop the tissue from repairing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The two words that must be spelt correctly are "tissue" (TIS + SUE — with a double 's') and "repairing" (RE + PAIR + ING).

◦ Correct: I can't stop the tissue from repairing.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 misspells "repairing" as "reparing" (the 'i' is dropped).

• Option 3 misspells "tissue" as "tisue" (only one 's').

• Option 4 misspells "repairing" as "repayring" (a wrong 'y' inserted).

NOTE

• "Tissue" in biology means a group of similar cells performing a common function; it also means a thin soft paper.

• Related spellings: repair, repairing, repaired, repairable, irreparable (note the different form of the last one).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Today I received a letter. Finally, I ______ back from him.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. heard.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The expression "hear back from someone" means to receive a reply or news from someone. Since the letter was already received, the past tense "heard" is required. (उत्तर मिलना)

◦ Correct: Today I received a letter. Finally, I heard back from him.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "herd" is a noun meaning a group of animals such as cattle (झुंड).

• Option 2 "hard" is an adjective/adverb meaning difficult or firm (कठिन).

• Option 4 "horde" means a large crowd or swarm of people (भीड़).

NOTE

• Homophone alert: heard (past of hear) vs herd (group of animals); hoard (a store) vs horde (a crowd).

• Verb forms: hear – heard – heard.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'no substitution required'.

(I wouldn't cross him if I was you, not) if you value your life.
option_2: I wouldn't has crossed him if I were you, not
option_3: I wouldn't had crossed him if I was you, not
option_4: I wouldn't cross him if I were you, not
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. I wouldn't cross him if I were you, not.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• This is a Type-2 (unreal/hypothetical) conditional: If + subject + past subjunctive (were), ... would + V1.

• In the subjunctive mood, "were" is used with all subjects, including "I". Hence "if I were you", never "if I was you".

◦ Correct: I wouldn't cross him if I were you, not if you value your life.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "No substitution required" is wrong because "if I was you" is not acceptable in standard formal English.

• Option 2 "I wouldn't has crossed" is doubly wrong — "would" must be followed by V1, and "has" is a finite form.

• Option 3 "I wouldn't had crossed him if I was you" mixes "would + had" and retains the wrong "was".

NOTE

• Conditional types: Type 1 — If + present, will + V1; Type 2 — If + past (were), would + V1; Type 3 — If + had + V3, would have + V3.

• "If I were you" is a fixed advice-giving formula.

question:
Choose the word that can substitute the given group of words.

Experiences that are very unpleasant or difficult
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Ordeal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• An "ordeal" is a very unpleasant, painful or prolonged difficult experience. (कठिन परीक्षा / यातनापूर्ण अनुभव)

◦ Example: The long journey through the desert was an ordeal for the travellers.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Pitfall" means a hidden danger or unsuspected difficulty (छिपा हुआ ख़तरा) — a trap, not an experience of suffering.

• Option 3 "Strident" is an adjective meaning loud and harsh in sound (कर्कश).

• Option 4 "Knack" means a special skill or talent for doing something easily (विशेष कौशल).

NOTE

• Historically, an "ordeal" was a medieval trial in which the accused was subjected to a painful test (trial by fire/water), the outcome deciding guilt or innocence.

• Synonyms: trial, tribulation, torment, suffering, nightmare.

question:
Choose the word that can substitute the given group of words.

To enter unlawfully upon the land of another
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Trespass.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Trespass" means to enter someone's land or property without permission or lawful right. (अनधिकार प्रवेश करना)

◦ Example: The board read, "Trespassers will be prosecuted."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Delinquent" is a noun/adjective for a person (usually young) who commits offences (अपराधी किशोर) — it names the offender, not the act of entering land.

• Option 3 "Transgression" is the general violation of a law, rule or moral code — too broad, and it does not specifically mean entering another's land.

• Option 4 "Culprit" means the person guilty of an offence (अपराधी) — again a person, not the act.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutes: encroach (to intrude gradually on someone's rights/property), poach (to hunt illegally on another's land), burglary (breaking into a house to steal).

question:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.

Rare
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Familiar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Rare" means not occurring often; uncommon, unusual, seldom found. (दुर्लभ)

• "Familiar" means well known, commonly seen or frequently encountered, which is the opposite of rare. (परिचित / सामान्य)

◦ Example: A rare bird versus a familiar sight.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Latent" means hidden or existing but not yet developed (गुप्त/सुप्त) — not an antonym of rare.

• Option 3 "Clarify" is a verb meaning to make clear — a different part of speech altogether.

• Option 4 "Extraordinary" means very unusual or remarkable — a synonym of rare, not its antonym.

NOTE

• Synonyms of rare: scarce, uncommon, infrequent, sparse, exceptional.

• Antonyms of rare: common, familiar, frequent, abundant, plentiful, ordinary.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Women ______ their male relatives to the battlefield for the purpose of tending the wounded and carrying away the dead.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. accompany.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Accompany" means to go somewhere along with someone. The sentence says the women went with their male relatives to the battlefield in order to nurse the wounded and remove the dead. (साथ जाना)

◦ Correct: Women accompany their male relatives to the battlefield ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "signify" means to indicate or be a sign of something (सूचित करना) — meaningless here.

• Option 2 "forsake" means to abandon or desert (त्याग देना) — the exact opposite of the intended sense, since the women stayed to help.

• Option 3 "justify" means to show something to be right or reasonable (औचित्य सिद्ध करना) — it does not fit "to the battlefield".

NOTE

• "Accompany" is used without a preposition before the object: "He accompanied me to the station" (not "accompanied with me").

• The related noun is companion, and "accompaniment" is used for music played along with a singer.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Dinner in the Great Hall that night (1) _______ a pleasant experience for Sunny. The (2) _______ about his shouting match with Umbridge had (3) _______ exceptionally fast even (4) _______ standards. He heard whispers all (5) _______ as he sat eating between Rob and Ravi.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. was not.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject "Dinner" is a singular noun, so it takes the singular verb "was", not the plural "were".

• The whole passage is narrated in the past tense ("had travelled", "He heard"), so the past form "was" is required, not the present "is".

• The negative "not" is needed because the following sentences show that the evening was unpleasant — everyone was whispering about him.

◦ Correct: Dinner in the Great Hall that night was not a pleasant experience for Sunny.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "were not" fails subject–verb agreement with the singular "Dinner".

• Option 2 "was neither" is wrong because "neither" requires a following "nor" to pair with.

• Option 4 "is not" breaks the past-tense narration of the passage.

NOTE

• Subject–verb agreement: singular subject → singular verb (Dinner was); plural subject → plural verb (Dinners were).

• Correlatives must be paired: neither ... nor, either ... or, not only ... but also.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Dinner in the Great Hall that night (1) _______ a pleasant experience for Sunny. The (2) _______ about his shouting match with Umbridge had (3) _______ exceptionally fast even (4) _______ standards. He heard whispers all (5) _______ as he sat eating between Rob and Ravi.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. news.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank needs a word that can travel fast and set people whispering. "News" (a report of a recent event) collocates naturally: "the news about his shouting match had travelled exceptionally fast". (समाचार / ख़बर)

◦ Correct: The news about his shouting match with Umbridge had travelled exceptionally fast ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "information" is possible in meaning but does not collocate idiomatically with "travelled fast" in this narrative sense; "news travels fast" is the fixed expression.

• Option 2 "sequence" means an order or series of events — it cannot "travel".

• Option 3 "account" means a narrative or description; an account is given, it does not spread by itself.

NOTE

• "News" is an uncountable noun ending in -s and takes a singular verb: "The news is good", "No news is good news".

• The proverb "Bad news travels fast" is the source of this collocation.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Dinner in the Great Hall that night (1) _______ a pleasant experience for Sunny. The (2) _______ about his shouting match with Umbridge had (3) _______ exceptionally fast even (4) _______ standards. He heard whispers all (5) _______ as he sat eating between Rob and Ravi.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. travelled.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The standard collocation with "news" is "news travels fast" — meaning it spreads quickly from person to person. After "had", the past participle "travelled" is used.

◦ Correct: The news ... had travelled exceptionally fast even by the institute's standards.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "drove" is the simple past of "drive"; after "had" the participle "driven" would be needed, and news does not "drive".

• Option 3 "migrated" refers to people, birds or animals moving from one region to another to settle — inappropriate for news.

• Option 4 "moved" is grammatically possible but far too vague; "news moved fast" is not the idiomatic expression.

NOTE

• British spelling doubles the 'l': travel – travelled – travelling; American spelling uses traveled / traveling. SSC papers generally follow British spelling.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Dinner in the Great Hall that night (1) _______ a pleasant experience for Sunny. The (2) _______ about his shouting match with Umbridge had (3) _______ exceptionally fast even (4) _______ standards. He heard whispers all (5) _______ as he sat eating between Rob and Ravi.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. by the institute's.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The fixed expression is "by ... standards", meaning judged according to those standards. Here the news spread fast "even by the institute's standards" — i.e., even when measured against how quickly gossip normally spread there.

• The singular possessive "institute's" is correct because only one institute is referred to.

◦ Correct: ... had travelled exceptionally fast even by the institute's standards.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "as the institute's" gives no sense of comparison of standards.

• Option 3 "of the institutes'" uses a plural possessive and the wrong preposition.

• Option 4 "at the institute" leaves "standards" without a possessor and breaks the idiom.

NOTE

• Possessive apostrophe: singular noun → -'s (the institute's rules); plural noun ending in -s → -' (the institutes' rules).

• Common expressions: "by any standards", "by today's standards", "by his own admission".

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Dinner in the Great Hall that night (1) _______ a pleasant experience for Sunny. The (2) _______ about his shouting match with Umbridge had (3) _______ exceptionally fast even (4) _______ standards. He heard whispers all (5) _______ as he sat eating between Rob and Ravi.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. around him.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The natural expression is "he heard whispers all around him", meaning on every side of him. "All around" is a fixed adverbial phrase of place.

◦ Correct: He heard whispers all around him as he sat eating between Rob and Ravi.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "revolving him" is wrong — "revolve" is intransitive in this sense; things revolve around something.

• Option 2 "surrounding him" would need "whispers surrounding him", but with "all" before the blank, "all surrounding him" is unidiomatic.

• Option 3 "rotating him" implies physically spinning him round — absurd in context.

NOTE

• Useful phrases: "all around" (on every side), "all over" (everywhere), "all along" (from the beginning), "all the same" (nevertheless).

question: Bangladesh does not share its boundary with which of the following Indian states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sikkim.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bangladesh shares its land boundary with five Indian states — West Bengal, Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram. Sikkim does not share any boundary with Bangladesh. (सिक्किम — बांग्लादेश से सीमा नहीं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The India–Bangladesh border is about 4,096 km long — India's longest international land boundary.

• West Bengal shares the longest stretch of this border (about 2,217 km); Meghalaya about 443 km, Mizoram about 318 km, Tripura about 856 km and Assam about 263 km.

• Sikkim shares its boundaries with China (Tibet), Nepal and Bhutan, and internally with West Bengal.

NOTE

• India's neighbours by land: Bangladesh, China, Pakistan, Nepal, Myanmar, Bhutan and Afghanistan. The Radcliffe Line separates India from Bangladesh and Pakistan.

question: According to Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS), BPL (Below Poverty Line) person aged 60 years or above are entitled to a monthly pension of ______ up to 79 years of age as of October 2022.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rs 200.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under the Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS), a BPL person aged 60–79 years is entitled to a central assistance of Rs 200 per month; on attaining 80 years, the amount rises to Rs 500 per month. (इंदिरा गांधी राष्ट्रीय वृद्धावस्था पेंशन योजना — 200 रुपये मासिक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• IGNOAPS is a component of the National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP), launched in 1995, administered by the Ministry of Rural Development.

• Other NSAP components: IGNWPS (widow pension, 40–79 years), IGNDPS (disability pension), National Family Benefit Scheme (NFBS) and Annapurna Scheme.

• States are free to top up the central contribution from their own funds, so the amount actually received varies from state to state.

NOTE

• The NSAP gives effect to Article 41 of the Constitution (a Directive Principle) — the right to public assistance in old age, sickness and disablement.

question: How many tax slabs are classified in the GST Bill?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Four.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Goods and Services Tax (GST) in India has four main tax slabs — 5%, 12%, 18% and 28%. (जीएसटी — चार कर स्लैब)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• GST was rolled out on 1 July 2017 through the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016. It replaced a host of indirect taxes such as excise duty, service tax and VAT.

• Types of GST: CGST (Central), SGST (State), UTGST (Union Territory) and IGST (Integrated, on inter-state supply).

• The GST Council (Article 279A) is the apex decision-making body, chaired by the Union Finance Minister, with state finance ministers as members.

• Essential items are taxed at 0% (exempt), while gold is taxed at a special rate of 3%; a compensation cess applies to luxury and sin goods.

NOTE

• France was the first country to adopt GST (1954). In India, the idea was first proposed by the Kelkar Task Force (2003).

question: Which among the following is not a part of Western Ghats?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahadeo Hills.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Mahadeo Hills are not a part of the Western Ghats — they lie in the Satpura Range in Madhya Pradesh (central India), where Dhupgarh (1,350 m), the highest peak of the Satpuras, is located. (महादेव पहाड़ियाँ — सतपुड़ा श्रेणी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Anaimalai Hills, Cardamom Hills and Nilgiri Hills all belong to the Western Ghats in South India.

• Anaimudi (2,695 m) in the Anaimalai Hills of Kerala is the highest peak of the Western Ghats and of peninsular India.

• The Western Ghats run about 1,600 km parallel to the west coast from the Tapi river to Kanyakumari, across Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu. They are a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the world's biodiversity hotspots.

NOTE

• Important passes of the Western Ghats: Thal Ghat, Bhor Ghat and Palghat (Palakkad Gap). The Palakkad Gap connects Kerala with Tamil Nadu.

question: Which British officer gave the order to open fire and led to the Jallianwala Bagh massacre?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Reginald Dyer.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Colonel Reginald Edward Harry Dyer ordered his troops to open fire on an unarmed gathering at Jallianwala Bagh, Amritsar, on 13 April 1919 (Baisakhi day), killing hundreds of people. (जनरल डायर — जलियाँवाला बाग हत्याकांड)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The crowd had assembled to protest against the Rowlatt Act (1919) and the arrest of leaders Dr Saifuddin Kitchlew and Dr Satyapal.

• In protest, Rabindranath Tagore renounced his knighthood and Sir Shankaran Nair resigned from the Viceroy's Executive Council.

• The Hunter Commission was appointed to enquire into the massacre. Udham Singh later shot Michael O'Dwyer (the Lieutenant Governor of Punjab) in London in 1940.

• The massacre was a direct trigger for the Non-Cooperation Movement (1920).

NOTE

• Warren Hastings was the first Governor-General of Bengal, Lord Cornwallis introduced the Permanent Settlement (1793), and Charles Metcalfe is known as the "Liberator of the Indian Press" (1835).

question: An image which cannot be obtained on a screen is called a ________ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is virtual image.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "virtual image" is formed when light rays only appear to meet after reflection or refraction — they do not actually converge. Hence a virtual image cannot be obtained (caught) on a screen. It is always erect. (आभासी प्रतिबिंब)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• A real image is formed when light rays actually meet; it can be caught on a screen and is always inverted (e.g., the image formed on a cinema screen or on the retina).

• A plane mirror always forms a virtual, erect and laterally inverted image of the same size, behind the mirror.

• A convex mirror and a concave lens always form virtual, erect and diminished images.

NOTE

• Mirror formula: 1/v + 1/u = 1/f; Lens formula: 1/v − 1/u = 1/f; Magnification: m = h'/h = v/u (mirror) and m = v/u (lens).

question: As of October 2022, how many fundamental duties are there in the Indian Constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 11.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• There are 11 Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution, listed in Article 51A of Part IV-A. (मौलिक कर्तव्य — 11)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Fundamental Duties were not in the original Constitution. Ten duties were added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.

• The 11th duty — that a parent or guardian shall provide opportunities for education to his child/ward between the ages of 6 and 14 years — was added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002.

• The idea of Fundamental Duties was borrowed from the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR.

• Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable, i.e., they cannot be enforced by the courts.

NOTE

• Part III — Fundamental Rights; Part IV — Directive Principles of State Policy; Part IV-A — Fundamental Duties (Article 51A).

question: Who among the following was the first musician ever to be awarded the Bharat Ratna?
solution_text:
The correct answer is M.S. Subbulakshmi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The legendary Carnatic vocalist M. S. Subbulakshmi became the first musician to be awarded the Bharat Ratna, in 1998. (एम. एस. सुब्बुलक्ष्मी — पहली संगीतकार, भारत रत्न 1998)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• She was also the first Indian musician to receive the Ramon Magsaysay Award (1974) and the first Indian to perform at the United Nations General Assembly (1966).

• Other musicians honoured with the Bharat Ratna: Ustad Bismillah Khan (2001), Pandit Ravi Shankar (1999), Pandit Bhimsen Joshi (2008) and Lata Mangeshkar (2001).

• The Bharat Ratna, instituted in 1954, is India's highest civilian award; the first recipients were C. Rajagopalachari, Dr S. Radhakrishnan and C. V. Raman.

NOTE

• Order of civilian awards: Bharat Ratna > Padma Vibhushan > Padma Bhushan > Padma Shri. A maximum of three Bharat Ratnas may normally be conferred in a year.

question: FIFA world cup 2022 is hosted by which country?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Qatar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The FIFA World Cup 2022 (the 22nd edition) was hosted by Qatar from 20 November to 18 December 2022. It was the first World Cup held in an Arab/Muslim country and the first played in the November–December window. (क़तर — फीफा विश्व कप 2022)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Argentina won the title, beating France in the final (3–3, then 4–2 on penalties) at the Lusail Stadium. Lionel Messi won the Golden Ball; Kylian Mbappé won the Golden Boot with 8 goals.

• The official mascot was "La'eeb" and the official match ball was "Al Rihla".

• FIFA (Fédération Internationale de Football Association) was founded in 1904 and is headquartered in Zurich, Switzerland.

NOTE

• The 2026 FIFA World Cup will be jointly hosted by the USA, Canada and Mexico and will feature 48 teams for the first time. Brazil has won the most titles (5).

question: Who wrote the treatise on politics, "Arthashastra"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kautilya.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Arthashastra, an ancient Sanskrit treatise on statecraft, economics, administration and military strategy, was written by Kautilya (also known as Chanakya or Vishnugupta), the chief minister of Chandragupta Maurya. (कौटिल्य — अर्थशास्त्र)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The text is divided into 15 books (adhikaranas) and describes the Saptanga theory of the state — the seven organs: Swami (king), Amatya (minister), Janapada (territory/people), Durga (fort), Kosha (treasury), Danda (army) and Mitra (ally).

• The manuscript was rediscovered and published by R. Shamasastry in 1909.

• Kautilya helped Chandragupta Maurya overthrow the Nanda dynasty and establish the Mauryan Empire around 322 BCE.

NOTE

• "Kadambari" was written by Banabhatta (who also wrote Harshacharita), and "Raghuvansham" is a mahakavya by Kalidasa, who also wrote Abhijnanashakuntalam and Meghadutam.

question: The stage of the embryo in which all the body parts can be identified is called ________ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is Foetus.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When the developing embryo reaches the stage at which all the body parts (organs and limbs) can be identified, it is called a "foetus" (fetus). In humans this stage begins around the end of the 8th–9th week of pregnancy. (भ्रूण / गर्भस्थ शिशु)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• A "zygote" is the single fertilised cell formed by the fusion of the sperm and the ovum (fertilisation). It divides repeatedly to form the embryo.

• "Ovulation" is the release of a mature egg from the ovary, usually around the middle of the menstrual cycle.

• The "uterus (womb)" is the organ in which the embryo/foetus develops; it is not a stage of development.

• The placenta connects the foetus to the mother's uterine wall for nutrition, gas exchange and waste removal.

NOTE

• Human gestation lasts about 9 months (280 days). Sequence: ovum + sperm → zygote → embryo → foetus → newborn.

question: The capital of Sangam kingdom 'Pandyas' was______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madurai.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Madurai was the capital of the Pandya kingdom of the Sangam Age. The Pandyas ruled the extreme south of the Indian peninsula. (मदुरै — पांड्य राजधानी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The three great kingdoms of the Sangam Age (roughly 300 BCE–300 CE) were the Cheras (capital Vanji/Karur, port Muziris), the Cholas (capital Uraiyur, port Puhar/Kaveripattinam) and the Pandyas (capital Madurai, port Korkai).

• The Pandyas were famous for pearl fishery at Korkai and for patronising the Tamil Sangams (literary academies) held at Madurai.

• Emblems: Chera — bow, Chola — tiger, Pandya — fish.

• Megasthenes and the Greek writers mention the Pandya kingdom; Ashoka's inscriptions also refer to the Cholas, Pandyas, Cheras and Satiyaputras.

NOTE

• The famous Meenakshi Temple at Madurai and classic Tamil works such as Silappadikaram and Manimekalai belong to this cultural sphere.

question: With reference to Buddhist architecture, what does chaitya mean?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Prayer Hall.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In Buddhist architecture, a "chaitya" is a prayer hall (shrine/assembly hall) which usually contains a stupa at its apsidal end where monks gathered for worship. (चैत्य — प्रार्थना गृह)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• A "vihara", by contrast, is the residence/monastery where the monks lived; it has cells arranged around a central courtyard.

• A "stupa" is a hemispherical mound built over the relics of the Buddha or a Buddhist saint. Its parts include the anda, harmika, yashti and chhatra.

• Famous rock-cut chaityas are found at Karle, Bhaja, Bedsa, Ajanta and Ellora (Maharashtra). The Karle chaitya is the largest.

NOTE

• The Great Stupa at Sanchi (Madhya Pradesh) was built by Ashoka and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Buddhist architecture flourished in the Mauryan, Sunga, Satavahana and Kushana periods.

question: Rulers belonging to Gurjara - Pratihara, Rashtrakuta and Pala dynasties fought for control over ________ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kannauj.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Gurjara-Pratiharas, the Rashtrakutas and the Palas fought a prolonged struggle for control over the city of Kannauj (in present-day Uttar Pradesh). This contest is famously called the "Tripartite Struggle" and lasted roughly for two centuries (8th–10th century CE). (कन्नौज — त्रिपक्षीय संघर्ष)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Kannauj had become the symbol of sovereignty over northern India after Harshavardhana made it his capital in the 7th century; it also commanded the fertile Ganga valley.

• Key rulers: Gurjara-Pratiharas — Nagabhata I, Vatsaraja, Nagabhata II, Mihir Bhoja; Rashtrakutas — Dhruva, Govinda III, Amoghavarsha, Krishna I (builder of the Kailasa temple at Ellora); Palas — Gopala, Dharmapala, Devapala.

• The Gurjara-Pratiharas ultimately gained lasting control of Kannauj.

NOTE

• The Pala rulers were Buddhists and founded the Vikramshila University; the Arab traveller Sulaiman described the three powers in his accounts.

question: For a person to be eligible to become the Vice-President of India, he must be of ______ years of age.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 35.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per Article 66 of the Constitution, a person must have completed 35 years of age to be eligible for election as the Vice-President of India. (उपराष्ट्रपति — न्यूनतम आयु 35 वर्ष)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Other qualifications: the person must be a citizen of India, qualified for election as a member of the Rajya Sabha, and must not hold any office of profit.

• The Vice-President is elected by an electoral college consisting of members of both Houses of Parliament (including nominated members) through proportional representation by means of a single transferable vote. State legislatures take no part.

• The Vice-President is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Article 64) and holds office for five years.

• India's first Vice-President was Dr S. Radhakrishnan.

NOTE

• The minimum age for President is also 35 (Article 58), for Lok Sabha MP/MLA it is 25, and for Rajya Sabha MP/MLC it is 30.

question: In India, roads are classified in the _______ classes according to their capacity.
solution_text:
The correct answer is six.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In India, roads are classified into six classes on the basis of their capacity — National Highways, State Highways, District Roads, Rural (Village) Roads, Border Roads and International Highways. (भारत में सड़कों का छह वर्गों में वर्गीकरण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• National Highways (NH) are constructed and maintained by the Central Government through the NHAI (National Highways Authority of India, established 1988); they form less than 2% of the road length but carry about 40% of the traffic.

• NH-44 (Srinagar to Kanniyakumari) is the longest national highway in India.

• Border Roads are built and maintained by the Border Roads Organisation (BRO, established 1960) in the strategic northern and north-eastern border areas.

• The Golden Quadrilateral connects Delhi–Mumbai–Chennai–Kolkata; the North–South corridor runs from Srinagar to Kanniyakumari and the East–West corridor from Silchar to Porbandar.

NOTE

• India has the second largest road network in the world after the USA. Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh have very extensive road networks.

question: Pandit Birju Maharaj was conferred with which of the following awards?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Padma Vibhushan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The legendary Kathak exponent Pandit Birju Maharaj was conferred the Padma Vibhushan in 1986, India's second highest civilian award. (पंडित बिरजू महाराज — पद्म विभूषण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Birju Maharaj (1938–2022) belonged to the Lucknow "Kalka-Bindadin" gharana of Kathak and was the son of Achhan Maharaj.

• He also received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award, the Kalidas Samman and a National Film Award for Best Choreography (for the film "Vishwaroopam"). He choreographed dances in films such as "Devdas", "Bajirao Mastani" and "Umrao Jaan".

• Kathak is the classical dance of North India (Uttar Pradesh), derived from the word "katha" (story); its main gharanas are Lucknow, Jaipur and Banaras.

NOTE

• The Shaurya Chakra is a peacetime gallantry award, ranking after the Ashoka Chakra and Kirti Chakra — not a civilian art award.

question: In MUDRA Yojana, what does 'M' stand for?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Micro.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• MUDRA stands for "Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency". Hence the letter 'M' stands for "Micro". (माइक्रो यूनिट्स डेवलपमेंट एंड रिफाइनेंस एजेंसी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY) was launched on 8 April 2015 to provide collateral-free loans up to Rs 10 lakh to non-corporate, non-farm small and micro enterprises.

• The loans are given in three categories: Shishu (up to Rs 50,000), Kishore (Rs 50,000 to Rs 5 lakh) and Tarun (Rs 5 lakh to Rs 10 lakh).

• Loans are disbursed through banks, NBFCs and Micro Finance Institutions; MUDRA itself is a refinance agency, a subsidiary of SIDBI.

NOTE

• The scheme comes under the Ministry of Finance and is aimed at "funding the unfunded" — promoting self-employment and micro-entrepreneurship.

question: Jhijhiya is a famous folk dance of Bihar and is performed in the mythological town of Mithila. This dance is performed by women only. The whole Navaratri 'nine nights' festival is celebrated to worship the three forms of Lord ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lakshmi, Parvati, and Saraswati.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• During Navaratri, the "nine nights" festival, the three principal forms of the Divine Mother — Lakshmi, Parvati (Durga) and Saraswati — are worshipped, three nights being devoted to each. Jhijhiya, the folk dance of the Mithila region of Bihar, is performed by women during this festival. (झिझिया — मिथिला, बिहार)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• In Jhijhiya, women dance balancing earthen pots (with many holes) containing lighted lamps on their heads, invoking Goddess Durga and seeking protection from evil.

• Other folk dances of Bihar: Jat-Jatin, Bidesia, Paika, Kajari, Sohar-Khilouna, Jumari and Domkach.

• Navaratri is celebrated in Chaitra (spring) and Ashwin (autumn, Sharad Navaratri, culminating in Vijayadashami/Dussehra).

NOTE

• The nine forms of Durga (Navadurga) are Shailaputri, Brahmacharini, Chandraghanta, Kushmanda, Skandamata, Katyayani, Kalaratri, Mahagauri and Siddhidatri.

question: The Central Government has recently launched YUVA 2.0 Scheme. It is a mentoring programme for young and budding authors below the age of ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 30.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "YUVA 2.0 (Young, Upcoming and Versatile Authors)" is a mentorship programme for young and budding authors below the age of 30 years, launched by the Ministry of Education in October 2022. (युवा 2.0 — 30 वर्ष से कम आयु के लेखक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• YUVA 2.0 was launched on the theme of "Democracy (institutions, events, people, constitutional values — past, present, future)".

• The scheme is implemented by the National Book Trust (NBT), India, under the Ministry of Education, as part of the Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav.

• Selected authors receive a consolidated scholarship of Rs 50,000 per month for six months and a 10% royalty on published books.

• The first edition, YUVA 1.0, was launched on 31 May 2021 on the theme of India's freedom struggle.

NOTE

• The National Book Trust was established in 1957 to promote reading and publishing in Indian languages; it organises the New Delhi World Book Fair.

question: The Indian National Congress passed Purna Swaraj resolution in 1929 under the presidentship of ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jawaharlal Nehru.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Purna Swaraj (complete independence) resolution was adopted at the Lahore Session of the Indian National Congress in December 1929, presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru. (लाहौर अधिवेशन 1929 — जवाहरलाल नेहरू)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• At the Lahore session, the tricolour flag of independence was unfurled by Nehru on the banks of the Ravi river, and 26 January 1930 was declared as the first Independence Day (Purna Swaraj Diwas).

• This is why 26 January was later chosen as the date on which the Constitution came into force (1950) — Republic Day.

• The resolution followed the rejection of the Nehru Report (1928) demand for Dominion Status and the failure of the Simon Commission to satisfy Indian aspirations.

• The Lahore session also authorised the launch of the Civil Disobedience Movement, which began with the Dandi March (12 March 1930).

NOTE

• Important Congress sessions: 1885 Bombay (W. C. Bonnerjee), 1907 Surat (split), 1916 Lucknow (Congress–League Pact), 1929 Lahore (Purna Swaraj), 1938 Haripura (Subhas Chandra Bose).

question: Which of the following god/goddess is NOT associated with Ratha Yatra festival of Puri, Odisha?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord Shiva.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Ratha Yatra of Puri (Odisha) is associated with the three deities — Lord Jagannath, his elder brother Lord Balabhadra and their sister Devi Subhadra. Lord Shiva is not associated with this festival. (रथ यात्रा — जगन्नाथ, बलभद्र, सुभद्रा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• During the Ratha Yatra the three deities are taken in three separate chariots from the Jagannath Temple to the Gundicha Temple — Nandighosha (Jagannath), Taladhwaja (Balabhadra) and Darpadalana/Devadalana (Subhadra).

• The festival falls on Ashadha Shukla Dwitiya (June–July) and the return journey is called Bahuda Yatra.

• The Jagannath Temple at Puri was built in the 12th century by the Eastern Ganga ruler Anantavarman Chodaganga Deva. It is one of the Char Dham pilgrimage sites.

NOTE

• The English word "juggernaut" (an unstoppable force) is derived from "Jagannath", from the huge chariots of this festival.

question: Which of the following layers is NOT one of the atmospheric layers of the earth?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Endosphere.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The atmosphere of the Earth is divided into five layers — Troposphere, Stratosphere, Mesosphere, Thermosphere (Ionosphere) and Exosphere. "Endosphere" is not an atmospheric layer. (एंडोस्फीयर — वायुमंडलीय परत नहीं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Troposphere (up to about 18 km at the equator, 8 km at the poles) — all weather phenomena occur here; temperature falls with height.

• Stratosphere (up to about 50 km) — contains the ozone layer, which absorbs harmful ultraviolet rays; ideal for jet aircraft flight.

• Mesosphere (up to about 80 km) — the coldest layer, where meteors burn up.

• Thermosphere/Ionosphere (up to about 400 km) — reflects radio waves back to earth, enabling long-distance communication.

• Exosphere — the outermost, rarefied layer merging into outer space.

NOTE

• The atmosphere is composed of about 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen and about 1% argon, carbon dioxide and other gases.

question: ______ hosted the World Games 2022 in July 2022.
solution_text:
The correct answer is United States of America.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The World Games 2022 (the 11th edition) were hosted by the United States of America at Birmingham, Alabama, from 7 to 17 July 2022. (विश्व खेल 2022 — संयुक्त राज्य अमेरिका)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The World Games is an international multi-sport event held every four years, one year after the Summer Olympics, for sports that are not part of the Olympic programme (such as tug of war, korfball, ju-jitsu, powerlifting, wushu, roller sports and lacrosse).

• The Games are organised by the International World Games Association (IWGA) with the patronage of the International Olympic Committee (IOC).

• The first World Games were held in Santa Clara, USA, in 1981. The event had originally been scheduled for 2021 but was postponed by a year because of the rescheduled Tokyo Olympics.

• The 2025 World Games were held in Chengdu, China.

NOTE

• India has won medals at the World Games in disciplines such as wushu, tug of war and billiards/snooker.

question: ______ describe the idea of evolution in his book, "The origin of species".
solution_text:
The correct answer is Charles Darwin.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Charles Darwin described the idea of evolution by natural selection in his famous book "On the Origin of Species", published in 1859. (चार्ल्स डार्विन — जीवों की उत्पत्ति)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Darwin's theory is based on natural selection — "survival of the fittest". He gathered his evidence during the voyage of HMS Beagle, especially from the finches of the Galapagos Islands.

• His other important work is "The Descent of Man" (1871).

• Jean-Baptiste Lamarck had earlier proposed the theory of "inheritance of acquired characters", which was later disproved.

NOTE

• Edward Jenner developed the smallpox vaccine (1796) and is called the father of immunology; Robert Brown discovered the cell nucleus (1831) and described Brownian motion; Aristotle is regarded as the father of biology/zoology.
